brief: brief-js163.md with js163-measurements.md, and the owner's direction of 2026-11-21 (detect the hardware and choose the best configuration automatically; fine-tuning allowed, never needed). On both UHD 630 nodes, in Jellyfin's image with jellyfin-ffmpeg, a 4K HDR re-encode done wholly on the GPU ran at 3.9 to 5.2 times real time for 0.16 to 0.28 CPU-seconds per second of film (4.1 to 7.2 on the processors), three at once at 1.5 to 2.0x each (video-processor tone map rows), at 0.97 to 1.47 times x264's bytes for equal SSIM on two fairly dark scenes; with an OpenCL tone map, one job at 3.85 to 3.97x for 0.5 to 0.7. No GPU tone map gives today's picture: the video processors' are about two thirds darker (VAAPI) and a third brighter (QSV) with no parameters; OpenCL with the hable curve is about a quarter darker, the same as jellyfin-ffmpeg's processor tone map. Today's colour tag options fail after GPU decode in ffmpeg 8; the same tags in the bitstream work.
tradeoff: Whether hardware encoding enters ahead of its place in the road, and what picture a viewer may be given for the speed: every measured GPU path changes an HDR film's brightness from the processor's.
entry: BL-040 is promoted on D-044's own reopen clause (a UHD 630 holds the job at 1.2x within twice x264's bytes), not on the request. JS-169 (measure, in jellyscale's own image, whether a GPU tone map with a set curve reaches the processor's picture; bytes on a bright scene and by a second measure; memory and jobs at once; the seam) enters at 20 and may run beside the builds ahead of it. JS-170 (first slice: Intel VAAPI/QSV, detected by a real test of each stage at start, chosen per job, processor otherwise) enters at 27 after JS-041 and JS-157, and moves to directly after JS-166 if JS-166 does not close the stall on processors or the dogfood counts a refusal for cores with every worker running. JS-054 keeps NVIDIA, AMD, hardware decode for processor streams and outputs above 1080 lines. 'Best configuration' is a rule of outcomes: the same picture first, then holding 1.2 times real time as measured on that worker, then no more than twice x264's bytes in a quality-targeted mode, then the least processor; otherwise the processor for that job, with the reason logged and counted (the HD 530 is the negative case). One film has one picture whatever the hardware: the driver video-processor tone maps are never used, by default or by override; a GPU tone map is accepted only within 5% (or one 8-bit code value, whichever is more) of the processor path's brightness above black and at SSIM 0.99 or above on three scenes; if no setting reaches that, the options return as a brief, among them moving the processor path to the shared curve, which would be a changed guarantee and is not taken here. Operators may set per worker hardware off, the device and the most hardware jobs at once, and nothing else; none is needed. Given up, by operators: the speed the video-processor tone maps have over the candidate path (up to a third) and their lower processor cost (0.16 to 0.28 CPU-seconds per second against 0.5 to 0.7, so 2 to 4 times), and with it some of the jobs one GPU node holds at once (three were measured on the rejected path, none yet on the candidate). Nothing by viewers. Unverified when decided: every figure in jellyscale's own image; the byte bound beyond two dark scenes of one film (SSIM margin about 0.0003); memory per job; the GPUs shared with other apps; whether any setting matches the picture; what brightness difference viewers notice (the 5% is the product owner's, to be argued with frames). Data that reopens it: JS-169 showing no path within the bound, or bytes past twice x264's on a bright scene; an operator's measured case where the automatic choice was wrong.
serves: PRODUCT.md: 'Only when nothing else works is the picture re-encoded, and an HDR film then looks right on an ordinary screen.' 'Any film plays, and plays well ... No codec, HDR format or subtitle track is second-class.' Operators 'want the server to be something they set up once and then mostly forget'. Goal 1: 'Playback never surprises a viewer.' The road, stage 4: hardware encoding. DOMAINS.md 22 and 23: a segment's frames depend on the spec hash, and the encoder family is in it.
